source_text: Ἐπειδὰν τοίνυν καὶ προφητοφόντας ἡμᾶς ἀπεκάλουν, ὅτι μὴ τοὺς ἀμετροφώνους αὐτῶν προφήτας ἐδεξάμεθα· τούτους γὰρ εἶναι φασὶν οὕς περ ἐπηγγείλατο τῷ λαῷ πέμψειν ὁ Κύριος· ἀποκρινάσθωσαν ἡμῖν πρὸς Θεοῦ ἔστι τὶς, ὦ βέλτιστοι, τούτων τῶν ἀπὸ Μοντανοῦ καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν λαλεῖν ἀρξαμένων, ὅς τις ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων ἐδιώχθη, ἢ ὑπὸ παρανόμων ἀπεκτάνθη; οὐδείς. οὐδέ γε τὶς αὐτῶν κρατηθεὶς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος ἀνεσταυρώθη; οὐ γὰρ οὖν· οὐδὲ μὴν οὐδὲ ἐν συναγωγαῖς Ἰουδαίων τῶν γυναικῶν τὶς ἐμαστιγώθη ποτὲ, ἢ ἐλιθοβολήθη; οὐδαμόσε οὐδαμῶς. ἄλλῳ δὲ θανάτῳ τελευτῆσαι λέγονται Μοντανός τε καὶ Μαξιμίλλα. τούτους γὰρ ὑπὸ πνεύματος βλαψίφρονος ἑκατέρους ὑποκινήσαντος, λόγος ἀναρτῆσαι ἑαυτούς· οὐχ’ ὁμοῦ κατὰ δὲ τὸν τῆς ἑκάστου τελευτῆς καιρὸν φήμη πολλή· καὶ οὕτω δὲ τελευτῆσαι καὶ τὸν βίον καταστρέψαι, Ἰούδα προδότου δίκην. καθάπερ καὶ τὸν θαυμαστὸν ἐκεῖνον τὸν πρῶτον τῆς κατ’ αὐτοὺς λεγομένης προφητείας οἷον ἐπίτροπον τινὰ Θεόδοτον, πολὺς αἱρεῖ λόγος, ὡς αἰρόμενόν ποτε καὶ ἀναλαμβανόμενον εἰς οὐρανοὺς, παρεκστῆναί τε καὶ καταπιστεῦσαι ἑαυτὸν τῷ τῆς ἀπάτης πνεύματι· καὶ δισκευθέντα, κακῶς τελευτῆσαι. φασὶ γοῦν τοῦτο οὕτω γεγονέναι. ἀλλὰ μὴ ἄνευ τοῦ ἰδεῖν ἡμᾶς ἐπίστασθαί τῶν τοιούτων νομίζομεν ὦ μακάριε. ἴσως μὲν γὰρ οὕτως, ἴσως δὲ οὐχ’ οὕτως τετελευτήκασι Μοντανός τε καὶ Θεόδοτος καὶ ἡ προειρημένη γυνή.
thought_title: No Montanist prophet was persecuted or martyred
orientation: The author is answering the Montanist charge that the church rejected the prophets whom the Lord promised to send, by asking whether any of the Montanist prophets suffered persecution or martyrdom.
pass_a_gloss: Since then they also called us prophet-killers, because we did not receive their immoderate-speaking prophets; for they say that these are the ones whom the Lord promised to send to the people; let them answer us before God, is there anyone, O best men, of these who began to speak from Montanus and the women, who was persecuted by Jews, or was killed by lawless men? No one. Was any of them, having been seized, crucified for the name? No indeed. Nor indeed was any of the women ever scourged in synagogues of Jews, or stoned? Nowhere in any way. But by another death Montanus and Maximilla are said to have died. For when a spirit that harms the mind had stirred each of them, a report says that they hanged themselves; not together, but at the time of each one's death there is much report; and that they died in this way and ended their life, after the manner of Judas the traitor. Just as also that wonderful Theodotus, the first, as it were, some steward of the prophecy called after them, a widespread report takes hold, that being lifted up at some time and being taken up into heavens, he fell into ecstasy and entrusted himself to the spirit of deceit; and having been hurled down, he died badly. They say indeed that this happened in this way. But not without seeing do we think that we know such things, O blessed one. For perhaps in this way, perhaps not in this way, Montanus and Theodotus and the aforementioned woman died.

choices.why: The compound means speaking without measure or restraint; a literal rendering preserves the charge of uncontrolled speech.
The adjective describes a spirit that damages the mind; a literal rendering keeps the causal force of the compound.
The middle infinitive with reflexive pronoun means to hang oneself; the literal rendering preserves the reported suicide.
The passive participle of δισκεύω means to be thrown or cast down; the literal rendering keeps the violent fall implied by the verb.
The term means one entrusted with management or oversight; rendering it as steward preserves the ironic description of Theodotus as a kind of manager of the prophecy.

bible_refs.note: Ἰούδα προδότου δίκην (after the manner of Judas the traitor) alludes to Judas' death by hanging.

pass_b_english: So when they called us prophet-killers because we did not receive their prophets who speak without measure—for they say these are the ones the Lord promised to send to the people—let them answer us before God: is there any one of these, my excellent friends, who began to speak from Montanus and the women, who was persecuted by Jews or killed by lawless men? No one. Was any of them seized and crucified for the name? No indeed. Was any of the women ever scourged in the synagogues of the Jews or stoned? Nowhere, in no way. Montanus and Maximilla are said to have died by a different death. For when a spirit that harms the mind stirred each of them, the report is widespread that they hanged themselves—not together, but each at the time of his or her own death. And so they died and ended their lives after the manner of Judas the traitor. Likewise, a widespread report holds that their so-called wonderful Theodotus, the first steward, so to speak, of their so-called prophecy, once when he was being lifted up and taken up into the heavens, fell into ecstasy and entrusted himself to the spirit of deceit, and having been hurled down, died miserably. But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them. For perhaps Montanus and Theodotus and the woman mentioned above died in this way, and perhaps not.

problems.why: The source says 'after the manner of Judas the traitor' without specifying a verse. The English adds '(Matthew 27:5)' as editorial gloss not in source, and Judas' death is differently reported in Matthew (hanged himself) vs Acts (fell headlong). The parenthetical creates false precision.
problems.fix: after the manner of Judas the traitor
problems.ruling: Source only says Ἰούδα προδότου δίκην; English adds “(Matthew 27:5)”, a citation not in the original.

problems.why: The English adds a specific New Testament citation that is not present in the Greek source.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical “(Matthew 27:5)” so the sentence reads “…the manner of Judas the traitor.”
problems.ruling: Greek has only 'Ἰούδα προδότου δίκην' (Judas the traitor's manner); no '(Matthew 27:5)' in source.

fixed: Removed editorial parenthetical '(Matthew 27:5)'; the source only says 'after the manner of Judas the traitor' (Ἰούδα προδότου δίκην) without a verse citation.

problems.why: The vocative plural βέλτιστοι addresses the opponents (the Montanists), not a general 'men'; English obscures this is direct address to the opponents being refuted.

fixed: Changed 'best of men' to 'you excellent fellows' because the source 'ὦ βέλτιστοι' is a vocative plural directly addressing the opponents, not a general reference to men.

problems.why: Priscilla named in intro only; in 2.1 'the women' then 'the woman mentioned above' unclear which woman, then Maximilla named.
problems.fix: Clarify Priscilla disappears from narrative; 'the woman' is Maximilla.

problems.quote: But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them. But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them.
problems.why: Exact sentence repeated verbatim; scribal or editorial error.

problems.quote: For perhaps Montanus and Theodotus and the woman mentioned above died in this way, and perhaps not.
problems.why: Contradicts preceding confident reports; 'without having seen them' leads to this odd retreat, but reader is confused about author's certainty.
problems.fix: Clarify: author reports widespread rumors but cannot verify.

problems.why: Sarcastic 'wonderful' (Greek thaumasios) not obvious; reader may take as praise.
problems.fix: Mark irony: 'the so-called wonderful Theodotus' or 'their wonderful Theodotus' [ironic].

problems.quote: once when he was being lifted up and taken up into the heavens, fell into ecstasy and entrusted himself to the spirit of deceit, and having been hurled down, died badly
problems.why: 'Taken up into the heavens' suggests ascension/rapture; but context implies he claimed this and fell. 'Died badly' is weak for likely 'died miserably/shamefully.'
problems.fix: Clarify: claimed heavenly rapture but fell and died miserably.

problems.quote: heresy of those called followers of Miltiades
problems.why: Same movement called by five different names across sections without explanation.
problems.fix: Note once that all terms refer to the same Montanist movement.

problems.quote: He even roused two other women
problems.why: Maximilla and Priscilla introduced vaguely, then referenced as 'the women' without naming them again.
problems.fix: Name Maximilla and Priscilla at first mention and clarify later references.

problems.quote: the followers of Themison silenced their mouths
problems.why: Montanist adherents called by different labels; Themison never explained.
problems.fix: Identify Themison as a Montanist leader at first mention.

problems.quote: But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them. But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them.
problems.why: Same sentence duplicated verbatim; likely scribal error.
'Wonderful' seems ironic or mistranslated; context is negative about a false prophet.
problems.fix: Use 'so-called wonderful' or note the irony.
